Safe home

Food and water

Create the ideal feeding space for your cat by following the principles of comfort and natural needs.

Contents
  1. 1. Choosing bowls
  2. 2. The ideal location
  3. 3. A comfortable height
  4. 4. Tip: bowl dimensions
  5. 5. Cleaning and caring for a cat drinking fountain

1. Choosing bowls

Material matters. Plastic accumulates bacteria and can cause feline acne. Recommended materials: glass, ceramic, and stainless steel.

2. The ideal location

Cats are creatures of habit and security. Never place food near the litter box.

  • A quiet corner free of drafts;
  • Away from noisy appliances;
  • A view of the room for a sense of safety.

3. A comfortable height

Bowls on a stand reduce strain on the neck and joints, especially in older cats. Tilting the bowl to the correct 15-degree angle makes swallowing more natural. Choose the height based on how tall your cat is while standing.

4

Tip: bowl dimensions

Tip

Bowl width: the inner diameter should be at least 1.5–2 times the width of the cat's face (including whiskers). For most adult cats, the optimal diameter is 15–18 cm; for large breeds (such as Maine Coons), 18–22 cm. If the diameter is under 12–13 cm, the cat's whiskers will keep brushing against the sides.

Bowl depth: 2–4 cm is ideal for both dry and wet food. The rim height should be about 1/2–3/4 of the height of the cat's face. Rims taller than 5–6 cm are only suitable for large food volumes and are less convenient for everyday feeding.

5

Cleaning and caring for a cat drinking fountain

Introduction

This is my personal experience of cleaning and caring for a cat drinking fountain. I want to tell you about the cleaning products, tools and cleaning methods I use myself.

The decision on how to clean the fountain and ensure your cat's comfort and wellbeing is up to you. Before using cleaning products, read the manufacturers' recommendations and make sure the products you choose are suitable for your fountain model.

1. Cleaning products and tools

Product No. 1

A dishwashing liquid that I use for the preliminary cleaning of the fountain. It helps remove slimy deposits and surface dirt.

  • Denkmit Ultra Sensitive
  • Sodasan Sensitive
  • Sonett Sensitiv
  • Ecover Zero
  • ATTITUDE Little Ones
  • and similar products in your city

Product No. 2

A product for treating plastic surfaces that come into contact with drinking water, which should be used according to the manufacturer's instructions. I use it diluted to soak individual parts of the fountain.

  • membraclean Drinking Water Treatment "Tierisch gut"
  • Purogene
  • Micropur Forte
  • Yachticon Aqua Clean
  • Milton
  • and similar products in your city. IMPORTANT — follow the manufacturer's instructions and its compatibility with the surface being treated, and rinse the surfaces thoroughly after treatment.

Tools you need

For cleaning I will need:

  • A small cleaning brush with medium-stiff bristles.
  • An ordinary sponge with a soft side.
  • A separate container that holds all the disassembled parts of the fountain.
  • A plate or another clean surface to keep the filters on for a while.

How to choose a cleaning brush?

It is important to choose a brush with the smallest possible diameter. It lets you clean narrow channels and hard-to-reach areas of the fountain and the pump.

2. Safety measures

When working with cleaning products, it is important to take the necessary precautions. Personally, I always wear protective gloves.

Before use, carefully read the instructions of the manufacturers of the products. Follow the recommended dilution ratios, contact times and other safety instructions.

Additional protective measures should be chosen according to the properties of the products used and the manufacturers' recommendations.

Do not mix different cleaning products with each other unless the manufacturers explicitly allow it.

Since the fountain is meant to supply drinking water to an animal, you need to make sure that the products used are suitable for cleaning the surfaces concerned. After treatment, rinse all parts thoroughly to remove any cleaning product residue.

3. Preparing the fountain

Before cleaning, I unplug the fountain and take it apart into separate parts.

All removable parts need to be separated from each other so that every surface, including hard-to-reach areas, can be cleaned thoroughly.

Before cleaning, you also need to remove the filters.

If you plan to reuse the filters, put them on a dry, clean surface while cleaning.

If you are going to fit a new filter, first rinse it under running water according to the manufacturer's instructions.

4. Preliminary cleaning

For the first stage of cleaning, I use product No. 1 and an ordinary sponge.

With the soft side of the sponge I clean all surfaces of the fountain. At this stage I remove slimy deposits and the main surface dirt.

It is important to clean not only the outer surfaces and easy-to-reach areas but also the internal parts where dirt can build up.

Cleaning the pump

I pay special attention to the pump, because slime and other dirt can also build up inside it.

To get to the pump rotor, you need to remove the outer protective grille. After that the rotor blades become accessible, and they can be carefully cleaned with the brush.

A brush with a small diameter lets you reach even hard-to-reach areas.

If necessary, I also carefully clean with the brush the outlet channel of the pump through which water flows into the fountain.

Be careful not to damage the internal components. Do not put the pump in water unless the manufacturer explicitly allows it.

5. Soaking individual parts

After the preliminary cleaning, I put the disassembled parts of the fountain in a separate container and add water with diluted product No. 2.

In my case I use the manufacturer's proportions for three liters of water in the container.

In my case I leave the parts in the solution for 20 minutes according to the manufacturer's instructions. All parts that can be soaked must be completely covered with liquid.

Please note: the dosage and contact time given are based on my personal experience. Before use, be sure to check the manufacturer's recommendations. In particular, check the recommended concentration, the contact time and the product's compatibility with the fountain's materials.

Do not soak the pump or other electrical components unless the manufacturer's instructions explicitly provide for it.

6. Thorough rinsing

After soaking, I rinse all parts thoroughly under running water several times.

At this stage it is important to remove all cleaning product residue and dissolved dirt from all surfaces and parts.

Pay special attention to the following areas:

  • Internal channels and narrow openings.
  • The rotor blades and accessible internal parts of the pump.
  • The outlet channel of the pump.
  • Areas where slime can build up.
  • Surfaces in direct contact with drinking water.

Before reassembling the fountain, make sure all parts have been rinsed thoroughly and no traces of cleaning products remain on them.

7. Fitting the filters

After cleaning, I put the filters back or use new ones.

If you have temporarily removed the filters and plan to reuse them, follow the manufacturer's storage recommendations. While cleaning, I put the filters on a dry, clean plate.

If you are fitting a new filter, first rinse it under running water according to the manufacturer's instructions.

This is especially important for activated carbon filters, because carbon dust may come out of them at the first rinse.

Whether a filter can be reused depends on its type and the manufacturer's recommendations. If the manufacturer requires the filter to be replaced, do not fit it again just because it looks clean.

8. How often I clean the fountain

I follow this maintenance schedule.

Once a week: a full manual cleaning of the fountain using both cleaning products and the brush.

Once every two weeks: replacing the filters — both the pump filter and the large white filter inside the fountain.

Important: replacement intervals may vary depending on the manufacturer, the water quality and how dirty it gets. So also follow the instructions for your fountain model.

9. Charging the fountain

In my fountain model, one battery charge usually lasts about two weeks in motion-sensor mode.

This is my personal experience. The actual battery life may differ depending on the model, the condition of the battery and how intensively it is used.

Important note

This article describes my personal approach to cleaning a cat drinking fountain and is not a universal recommendation for all models.

Before using cleaning products, check whether they are suitable for the materials of your device and safe for surfaces that come into contact with your cat's drinking water.

The instructions of the manufacturers of the fountain, the filters and the cleaning products always take priority.
